intro: Monday June 23. All three macro gates failed simultaneously: VIX 17.53 (above 17 gate), DXY 100.90 (above 100 gate, worsening), SPX futures -1.43% (below 7,460 gate floor). Three structural events define the session: (A) BTC double-bottom ($62,255–$62,313) breached at $61,926 intraday — Day 1 stop-clock near-certain at June 23 UTC midnight; reduce 50% below $63,000 immediately; (B) SK Hynix circuit breakers triggered twice on KOSPI (KOSPI -4.6%); intraday ATH ₩3,000,000 hit before -12% reversal; stop ₩2,540,000 intact; conviction downgraded to medium; (C) NVDA Annual Meeting override NOW ACTIVE — DXY gate has failed on both June 22 and June 23; add NVDA in the June 23 US session before June 24 open (Annual Meeting 9 AM PT). The ideas below are calibrated for the June 24 session — the most important trading day of the post-FOMC cycle: NVDA Annual Meeting at open (9 AM PT) + Micron Q3 earnings after close (EPS $19.95 est., revenue $34.66B est., gross margin >80%). Three scenarios for June 24: (A) Micron beats revenue $34.66B AND guides HBM above consensus → AI memory re-rates, SK Hynix gap-up June 25 KST, NVDA extends post-Annual-Meeting gains; (B) Micron meets but doesn't raise HBM guidance → mixed, hold NVDA/SK Hynix, monitor BTC Day 2 UTC; (C) Micron misses revenue $34.66B → full AI memory de-rating, exit MU immediately, re-evaluate SK Hynix thesis.

ideas.name: NVIDIA
ideas.idea: Annual Meeting override now active — add in the June 23 US session; override requires add before June 24 open (Annual Meeting 9 AM PT) regardless of DXY gate status; June 24 dual catalyst (Annual Meeting + Micron Q3) is the compound conviction anchor.
ideas.why: The override rule was specifically designed for the scenario now in force: DXY gate failed on June 22 (100.76) AND June 23 (100.90) with the Annual Meeting date arriving. The June 24 compound event — Jensen Huang's first post-FOMC public AI capex commentary at 9 AM PT simultaneously with Micron Q3 ($34.66B revenue est. / $19.95 EPS est. / >80% gross margin / HBM sold-out through 2027) after close — is the most powerful single-day AI semiconductor catalyst of the 2026 cycle. VIX 17.53 and SPX futures -1.43% increase intraday execution risk; use limit orders at $207–$213 rather than market open. 50-DMA support ~$206.74 is the technical floor. The June 23 broad market selloff (KOSPI -4.6%, BTC double-bottom breach) may provide a lower-price entry within the $205–$215 add zone during the US session.
ideas.trigger: Execute in June 23 US session: limit orders $207–$213. Do NOT wait for DXY gate clearance — the override eliminates the gate requirement for this event. If NVDA opens below $205 on June 23 (SPX futures -1.43% impact): buy at $205 as the 50-DMA confluence. Stop $195 daily close. June 24: hold through Annual Meeting AND through Micron Q3 after-close results before deciding on exit.
ideas.risk: 30Y closes above 5.00% before June 24 AND Micron misses on HBM revenue → full reassessment; Jensen June 24 Annual Meeting commentary indicates AI capex slowdown (unexpected reversal of prior hyperscaler signals); DXY breaks above 102 on hawkish June 23 Fed speaker comments.

ideas.name: Micron Technology
ideas.idea: June 24 Q3 earnings after close — EPS $19.95 est. / revenue $34.66B est. / gross margin >80%; highest-ever Micron consensus bar; HBM sold-out through 2026–2027; VIX 17.53 and SPX futures -1.43% create the intraday pullback that is the pre-earnings entry window.
ideas.why: Micron Q3 consensus has been revised up 3.1% in 30 days and now reflects near-record-high expectations for HBM revenue and gross margin. A Micron beat-and-raise on June 24 simultaneously validates: (1) NVDA's Blackwell/Vera Rubin HBM supply chain, (2) SK Hynix's 58% HBM market-share premium, (3) AI hyperscaler capex durability through 2027, and (4) the overall AI semiconductor bull thesis. The June 23 broad market selloff (SPX futures -1.43%) creates lower intraday prices in MU before the June 24 fundamental event — the framework calls for buying fundamentally-driven catalysts at macro-driven discounts. HBM is confirmed sold-out through 2026–2027 by multiple sources; Micron Q3 is the official public confirmation of that constraint.
ideas.trigger: June 23 intraday: buy MU at $95–$110 as market-wide selloff creates the entry window. If MU falls below $100 intraday on SPX futures contagion → buy at $98–$100 as the best pre-earnings entry. Stop $90 daily close. Post-June-24 results: hold for momentum leg if revenue beats $34.66B AND Q4 HBM guidance raises; exit immediately if HBM revenue misses or guidance cuts.
ideas.risk: MU misses the $34.66B / $19.95 EPS / >80% gross margin triple bar; management warns Q4 2026 HBM demand from enterprise budget pressure; Samsung gains NVIDIA HBM market share faster than expected before MU Q4 guidance period.

ideas.name: SK Hynix (000660.KS)
ideas.idea: Hold core long; do NOT add during circuit-breaker session; June 25 KST KOSPI open is the primary Micron Q3 read-through session — arrive positioned in core before June 24 KST close; stop ₩2,540,000 intact at estimated ₩2,569,000 close.
ideas.why: SK Hynix's June 23 KST session was a parabolic ATH (₩3,000,000 — 25-year record surpassing Samsung) followed by a circuit-breaker reversal to an estimated -12% close (~₩2,569,000). Stop at ₩2,540,000 is intact (~₩29,000 margin). The structural thesis — 58% HBM global market share, NVIDIA supply lock through 2030, HBM4E 12-layer confirmed — is unchanged. Samsung HBM4E competition reports cite no confirmed NVIDIA qualification. The June 23 reversal is the pattern of a local top after a parabolic move, not a structural de-rating. If Micron Q3 beats on June 24 (revenue $34.66B / HBM guidance above consensus), the June 25 KST KOSPI session is the primary recovery and extension event — sell-side PT revisions above ₩3,000,000 are mandatory.
ideas.trigger: Hold core long through June 25 KST. Do NOT add in June 23–24 KST sessions (circuit-breaker uncertainty + Samsung competition headline overhang). Next tactical add: June 25 KST open if Micron beats revenue $34.66B AND guides HBM demand above consensus. Stop: ₩2,540,000 (two consecutive KST daily closes below required for execution).
ideas.risk: Samsung announces confirmed NVIDIA HBM4E qualification before SK Hynix; Micron Q3 HBM revenue miss with downward Q4 2026 guidance (direct negative read-through June 25 KST); two consecutive KOSPI closes below ₩2,540,000 trigger full exit.

ideas.name: Bitcoin
ideas.idea: Double-bottom structural support ($62,255–$62,313) breached at $61,926 intraday; current $62,369 is $1,131 below $63,500 stop level; framework action: reduce 50% immediately (below $63,000 threshold); Day 1 of new stop-clock near-certain at June 23 UTC midnight; Day 2 = June 24 UTC close (full exit if closes below $63,500).
ideas.why: BTC's $62,255–$62,313 double-bottom was the structural floor that survived two prior Day 1 stop-clock events (June 18 and June 21). The June 23 intraday breach at $61,926 is the first penetration of this two-session structural anchor. The breach, combined with KOSPI -4.6% circuit breakers and all three macro gates simultaneously failed, signals that the institutional bid at the double-bottom has been exhausted. The framework's two-consecutive-close rule requires Day 2 for full exit, but the prescribed action for a breach below $63,000 is already a 50% reduction — that action is mandatory regardless of the two-close timing. Current price $62,369 offers the reduction entry before potential further deterioration toward the $60,000–$62,000 re-entry zone.
ideas.trigger: Reduce 50% at current market ($62,000–$62,500 range) — do not wait for June 23 UTC close. Remaining 50%: monitor June 24 UTC midnight close. If June 24 UTC closes below $63,500 → FULL EXIT, no exceptions, no averaging down. Re-entry conditions: two consecutive UTC closes above $62,000 in the $60,000–$62,000 zone.
ideas.risk: BTC reverses sharply above $63,500 before June 23 UTC close (stop clock fails to activate, double-bottom breach was a wick below support rather than a structural close); IBIT inflows resume on June 23 (institutional accumulation signal that counters retail stop-hunt thesis); DXY closes below 100 on June 23 (removes last macro headwind).

ideas.name: SpaceX
ideas.idea: Step aside maintained; June 22 Day 1 close-above-$185 attempt failed ($165.78 actual close); $20B bond distribution overhang (1–2 weeks) is the supply headwind; re-entry gate $185 requires +15.6% from ~$160 premarket; watch from the sidelines.
ideas.why: The June 22 IG ratings gap-up did NOT materialize into a sustained close: SPCX June 22 actually closed at ~$165.78, far below the $185 re-entry gate, resetting the two-consecutive-close clock to zero. The $20B bond distribution (announced at IPO; 1–2 week clearing window) is creating sustained near-term supply overhang that overwhelms the demand signal from the IG ratings. At ~$160 premarket, SPCX is 11% below even the June 22 close — the bond distribution impact is accelerating. The structural thesis remains intact (Moody's Baa1 / Fitch BBB+ / S&P BBB permanent franchise floor, Starlink $20B+ revenue trajectory, Cursor AI layer) but the two-consecutive-close re-entry discipline exists exactly for this type of supply-driven near-term pressure. The September 2 first earnings is the next structural re-entry catalyst.
ideas.trigger: Watch only. Re-entry conditions: TWO consecutive daily closes above $185 on above-average volume (>100M shares), ideally after the $20B bond distribution period clears (est. 1–2 weeks from IPO date). September 2 first earnings = primary re-engagement catalyst if $185 gate not cleared before then. Do NOT buy below $185 on any timeline.
ideas.risk: Bond distribution completes faster than expected (1 week rather than 2), removing the supply overhang and creating a rapid gap to $185; Elon Musk Starship progress announcement before bond distribution clears triggers a volume-driven two-close sequence at lower levels.

ideas.name: Meta Platforms
ideas.idea: Downgraded from buy to watch for June 23 session — VIX 17.53 (above 17 gate) and all three macro gates simultaneously failed; hold existing position but do not add new; June 24 Micron Q3 is the AI capex validation that would upgrade conviction to medium.
ideas.why: Meta's fundamentals remain the cleanest in big tech (self-funded AI, lowest forward multiple in Mag-7 post-FOMC selloff, international advertising revenue benefiting from eventual DXY decline). But June 23 is not the day to add new exposure: VIX 17.53 is above the 17 gate, DXY 100.90 is worsening rather than improving, SPX futures -1.43% signal broad risk-off, and SK Hynix circuit breakers add global equity uncertainty. The downgrade from 'buy' to 'watch' is a framework compliance call, not a fundamental change — META at ~$540–$545 (estimated from SPX futures -1.43% impact on June 22 close) is still an attractive 2–3 quarter vehicle. June 24 Micron Q3 beat-and-raise on AI capex → upgrade back to medium conviction and add.
ideas.trigger: June 24: if Micron Q3 beats AND guides above consensus on HBM demand → upgrade to medium conviction and add META at market ($540–$560); June 24 post-NVDA Annual Meeting Jensen commentary confirming AI capex → add concurrently. Stop $530 daily close.
ideas.risk: AI capex cycle peak signals in Micron Q3 guidance (directly removes META's advertising AI ROI thesis); DXY breaks above 102 (full international ad revenue headwind); 30Y tests 5.00% triggering multiple compression across all long-duration growth names.

ideas.name: SPDR Energy Select Sector ETF
ideas.idea: Short thesis accelerating — KOSPI circuit breakers + global risk-off on June 23 compounds the structural Brent headwind; Hormuz reopening on 30-day timeline intact; H2 sell-side energy estimate cuts have not begun; Brent ~$80.20.
ideas.why: The June 23 macro environment is additive to the XLE short thesis: global risk-off (KOSPI -4.6%, SPX futures -1.43%, BTC structural break) is incrementally bearish for commodity demand expectations. Brent at ~$80.20 remains $6–9 below the $87–$90 embedded in H2 2026 sell-side energy equity models. The Hormuz mine-clearance timeline (30-day from Iran ceasefire) is on track — commercial shipping normalizing as mines are cleared reduces the supply-disruption premium. H2 2026 estimate cuts have not yet appeared in consensus; the gap between Brent reality ($80) and model assumptions ($87–$90) creates a 6–9 week window of sequential estimate cuts as sell-side desks update. Risk-off June 23 session: any Brent bounce to $82–$84 on spurious Hormuz delay headlines is the best short entry.
ideas.trigger: If XLE opens at $53–$56 with Brent below $83 on June 23 → initiate or add to short. Brent bounce to $82–$84 on Hormuz mine-clearance delay headline = premium short entry opportunity. Cover only on two consecutive Brent closes above $90.
ideas.risk: Iran ceasefire collapses before mine-clearance completes; Hormuz mine-clearance delayed beyond 60 days; OPEC+ emergency production cut announcement; non-Hormuz supply shock (Libya, Nigeria) pushes Brent above $90.
